name: K-Means Clustering
description: K-Means is a centroid-based clustering algorithm that partitions data into k clusters by minimizing within-cluster variance. It assigns each data point to the nearest centroid and iteratively updates centroids until convergence. One of the most popular and scalable clustering methods.

concept.objective: Minimize sum of squared distances from points to their cluster centroids
concept.centroid: Mean of all points in cluster
concept.algorithm: Lloyd's algorithm - iterative refinement of centroids
concept.convergence: When centroids stop moving or change is below threshold
concept.explanation: Randomly initialize k centroids. Assign each point to nearest centroid. Recalculate centroids as mean of assigned points. Repeat until convergence.

idealScenarios: When number of clusters is known or can be estimated

init.impact: k-means++ provides better starting points, faster convergence

maxIter.impact: Prevents infinite loops on non-converging cases

nInit.description: Number of times to run with different centroid seeds
nInit.impact: Higher = better solution but slower; picks best result

algorithm.impact: Elkan faster for dense data with small k

preprocessing: Consider dimensionality reduction (PCA) for high-dim data
determineK: Elbow Method: plot inertia vs k, find elbow point
Silhouette Analysis: measure cluster separation quality
Gap Statistic: compare to random uniform distribution
training: Assignment step: assign each point to nearest centroid
Update step: recalculate centroids as cluster means
Repeat until convergence or max iterations
evaluation: Silhouette Score: (-1 to 1, higher is better)

complexity.timeTraining: O(n × k × d × i) where n=samples, k=clusters, d=dimensions, i=iterations
complexity.timePrediction: O(k × d) - assign to nearest centroid
complexity.scalability: Excellent - linear in n, works with large datasets
complexity.interpretability: Medium - centroids interpretable as cluster prototypes

pros: Fast and scalable to large datasets
cons: Assumes spherical clusters of similar size

variants.kMedoids: Uses actual data points as centers (more robust to outliers)

determiningK.elbowMethod: Plot inertia vs k, look for elbow
determiningK.silhouette: Average silhouette width for each k
